body:
# Kārttikeya, spelled the way the sources wrote it
There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *kartikeya*. This is the file on how **Kārttikeya** replaced it.

Kārttikeya's myths are the war-god's perfect résumé: born for one battle, victorious in seven days, and never outgrown by the cult that made him its own. The gods, unable to face the demon Tāraka, needed Śiva's son — but Śiva would not marry.  From the fire of his third eye the seed fell through Agni and the Gaṅgā to the reeds, where the six Kṛttikā stars (the Pleiades) found and nursed the child.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Kārttikeya
- **ASCII form:** kartikeya
- **Meaning:** "Son of Krittika"
- **Domain of influence:** War, Commander of Gods
- **Pantheon:** Sanskrit
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** कार्त्तिकेय
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 129 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Kārttikeya** to *kartikeya* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **a → ā** — Long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Kārttikeya** lives at [/sites/kartikeya/](/sites/kartikeya/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/kartikeya/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/kartikeya/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/kartikeya/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Kārttikeya** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Defense, Military & Security** — The commander of the gods armies; the week-old general.
- **Faith & Spiritual Organizations** — The six-faced war god who rides his peacock still through the temples of two nations that call him their own.
- **Travel, Tourism & Place Branding** — Palani, Kataragama, Batu Caves — his hills are pilgrimage infrastructure.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Sanskrit tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Rig Veda](/texts/rig-veda/) and [Ramayana](/texts/ramayana/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/kartikeya/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
